item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is the preferable patch because its replay support is more narrowly and maintainably implemented, and its Upload validation and documentation are clearer. However, both patches materially violate the frozen contract by duplicating FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it and by changing global raw/retry behavior.","reasons":["B isolates seekable-body replay in enableBodyReplay, avoids seeking to the end solely to calculate Content-Length, and gracefully leaves an unusable seeker non-replayable. A can make a previously sendable request fail before its first attempt when SeekCurrent or SeekEnd is unsupported.","B returns distinct validation errors for an empty filename and nil content, making the API easier to diagnose than A's combined error.","B directly tests the established multipart helper's field name, filename, content, and validation behavior, while its Upload tests verify multipart encoding and replayed content.","A has the stronger realistic retry test—it uses an actual os.File and compares complete multipart bodies—but that advantage does not outweigh its more intrusive and failure-prone raw replay implementation."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly and duplicates Add's option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data behavior, contrary to the explicit requirement to route through FilesService.Add.","The RawClient change expands scope and changes Add, Update, and Raw.Do body ownership/retry semantics despite the contract explicitly prohibiting unrelated retry refactoring and requiring Add behavior to remain unchanged.","Seeking to the end can reject valid read-seekers that can report/reset their current position but do not support SeekEnd, changing formerly successful one-shot requests into immediate errors and potentially triggering reader side effects before transmission last time check: typo? no final already? keep JSON valid.Continue risks array concise. No source reader test."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its machinery, violating the central reuse requirement and creating future divergence risk.","The global RawClient replay change alters Add, Update, and Raw.Do behavior and reader-closing semantics outside the authorized scope.","The Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than an os.File or forward-only source reader, so it is less representative of the reported streamed-content scenario; no test explicitly exercises source-reader failure propagation."]}
